speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), and are you currently experiencing any abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and severe pruritus, I need to check for signs of cholestasis; have you noticed any darkening of your urine or pale, clay-colored stools? I will also need to rule out viral hepatitis given your sexual history, so REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, Hepatitis_B_and_C_Serology, and Anti-Mitochondrial_Antibody.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Panel: Total Bilirubin 1.5 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 460 U/L, AST 75 U/L, ALT 78 U/L. Anti-Mitochondrial_Antibody: Negative. Hepatitis_B_and_C_Serology: NOT FOUND.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated alkaline phosphatase with negative viral and autoimmune markers, combined with your history of ulcerative colitis, strongly suggests Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. REQUEST TEST: MRCP.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRCP is unavailable, let's focus on your current symptoms: have you experienced any unintended weight loss, fever, or night sweats recently? I will also REQUEST TEST: IgG levels and request an abdominal ultrasound to look for biliary dilation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: IgG levels: NOT FOUND. Abdominal Ultrasound: Thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of bile duct thickening and dilatation, combined with your history of ulcerative colitis and cholestatic liver enzymes, are highly characteristic of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
